proposals.evidence: The survey explicitly defines its fraction compounds as the larger number in ablative/instrumental plural plus the smaller number, and prints pāndžundār-ištār/pāndž-ištār 'four fifth' (p. 138 §3.5.3.1). Its five-member is the separately installed Zargari pānj 'five' (already CDIAL 7655; Turner European Romani panǰ), and the four-member is iśtār 'four' (already CDIAL 4655 §1; Turner European Romani štar). The -undār ending is source case morphology, not an independent etymon. This is a synchronic two-component fraction, not a proposed reflex of a fused Sanskrit fraction. Original PDF, exact source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
